title: A hostel vending machine with explicit states

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own vending machine design case and kata, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

scenario: The hostel common room is getting a snack vending machine that takes coins and gives change. Design the controller's classes and code it so that every command behaves correctly in every state: money inserted or not, item in stock or not, enough credit or not.

clarifying_questions.a: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100 rupee values; anything else is refused.

clarifying_questions.q: Does the machine always have change?
Can a student buy two items with one insertion?
clarifying_questions.a: No: a sale returns all remaining credit as change.
Returns all credit; with no credit it says there is nothing to refund.

functional: Stock items with a price and quantity
Sell an item with change, or explain why not

non_functional.name: Correctness
non_functional.target: no item dispensed without full payment; credit never lost

non_functional.name: Clarity
non_functional.target: every command defined in every state

entities.name: Machine
entities.responsibility: Holds the state (IDLE or PAID), the credit and the stock; each command checks the state first.

entities.name: Item record
entities.responsibility: Price and quantity of one product.

entities.name: Driver (Main)
entities.responsibility: Parses commands and validates coins and numbers.

patterns.name: State machine (explicit state field)
patterns.why: Writing the states down (IDLE, PAID) and checking them first in each command makes every command's behaviour in every state visible and testable.

patterns.name: Guard clauses
patterns.why: Each refusal returns early with a clear message, so the success path at the end is short and safe.

diagram.alt: State diagram: IDLE goes to PAID on INSERT; PAID stays PAID on INSERT or a refused SELECT; PAID returns to IDLE on a successful SELECT (dispense with change) or CANCEL (refund).

data.source:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> IDLE
  IDLE --> PAID: INSERT
  PAID --> PAID: INSERT / refused SELECT
  PAID --> IDLE: SELECT ok (dispense + change)
  PAID --> IDLE: CANCEL (refund)

kata.io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `STOCK <item> <price> <qty>` | `<item>: <qty in stock> at <price>` (re-stocking keeps the first price) |
| `INSERT <coin>` | `credit <total>` |
| `SELECT <item>` | `dispense <item>, change <c>`, `error: insert money first`, `error: <item> unavailable`, or `error: need <n> more` |
| `CANCEL` | `refund <credit>` or `nothing to refund` |

Coins: 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100. Prices and quantities 1-10000. Anything else: `error: bad command <line>`.

change_request.description: The warden wants to change prices without emptying the machine. Add `PRICE <item> <price>`: prints `<item> now <price>`, or `error: <item> unavailable` for an item never stocked. Credit already inserted is untouched.

rubric.criterion: Kata tests pass, including the price change.
States are explicit and each command checks the state before acting.
Credit is never lost: refused selections keep credit, sales return change, cancel refunds.
Repricing touches only the item record and the driver.
Guard clauses and naming (AI feedback, advice only).

concept_checks.stem: Credit is 20 and the item costs 35. What should SELECT do?
options: Refuse with 'need 15 more' and keep the 20 credit
concept_checks.explanation: A refused selection leaves the state and credit as they were.

concept_checks.stem: In which state is SELECT refused with 'insert money first'?
concept_checks.explanation: With no credit, nothing can be sold.

concept_checks.stem: Why make the state an explicit field instead of checking credit > 0 everywhere?
options: It names the states, so every command can be specified and tested per state
concept_checks.explanation: Explicit states make the behaviour table visible.

concept_checks.stem: Inserting 50 for an item of 20 gives what?

follow_ups: What if the machine runs out of coins for change? Add a coin inventory and refuse sales it cannot change.
Model a third state, DISPENSING, for a motor that can jam.
Show the state pattern with one class per state and compare it with the enum version.

revision_card.front: Vending machine LLD: states, transitions, and the money rule?
revision_card.back: IDLE --INSERT--> PAID; PAID --SELECT ok--> IDLE (dispense + change); PAID --CANCEL--> IDLE (refund); refused SELECT keeps state and credit. Check the state first in every command (guard clauses).
